dedupe_keys.name: transims simulation of the new orleans transit assisted hurricane evacuation plan

description: Hana Naghawi and Brian Wolshon of Louisiana State University modelled the transit-assisted mass evacuation plan that New Orleans prepared after Hurricanes Katrina and Rita exposed the lack of plans for people without cars. Published in the Journal of Transportation Safety and Security in 2010, it is one of the first systematic simulations of transit-based evacuation strategies. They used TRANSIMS, the agent-based Transportation Analysis and Simulation System, to simulate a two-day evacuation, comparing two alternative transit evacuation routing plans under four network loading scenarios, with average travel time and total evacuation time as measures. Transit evacuation was most effective when run during the lull of the car-based evacuation, off-peak and overnight, giving up to 10% lower overall travel time and up to 45% lower total evacuation time than under peak conditions, and routing buses on alternative arterials also helped. Coverage: the New Orleans region and its City-Assisted Evacuation Plan. Access: the journal article; the abstract is public. Licence and cost: publisher copyright, closed access. Caveats: a planning simulation with assumed demand, not an observed evacuation. It supports emergency response, agent-based and network flow studies of evacuation for carless populations. It relates to the Hurricane Katrina New Orleans hospitals case study and the BusMezzo transit simulator in the catalogue.
